barbarian.name: Barbarian
bard.name: Bard
bard.spellcasting.1.name: Cantrips
bard.spellcasting.1.desc:
You know two cantrips of your choice from the Bard spell list. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list.
When you reach Bard levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Bard Features table.
bard.spellcasting.2.name: Spell Slots
bard.spellcasting.2.desc: The Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.
bard.spellcasting.3.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
bard.spellcasting.3.desc:
You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Bard spell list. Charm Person, Color Spray, Dissonant Whispers, and Healing Word are recommended.
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Bard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Bard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Bard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
If another Bard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Bard spells for you.
bard.spellcasting.4.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
bard.spellcasting.4.desc: Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots.
bard.spellcasting.5.name: Spellcasting Ability
bard.spellcasting.5.desc: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Bard spells.
bard.spellcasting.6.name: Spellcasting Focus
bard.spellcasting.6.desc: You can use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells.

warlock.name: Warlock
warlock.spellcasting.1.name: Cantrips
warlock.spellcasting.1.desc:
You know two Warlock cantrips of your. Eldritch Blast and Prestidigitation are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table.
warlock.spellcasting.2.name: Spell Slots
warlock.spellcasting.2.desc:
The Warlock table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1-5. The table also shows what the level of those slots are, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell Charm Person, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.
warlock.spellcasting.3.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
warlock.spellcasting.3.desc:
You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. Charm Person and Hex are recommended.
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1-3.
If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Warlock spells for you.
warlock.spellcasting.4.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
warlock.spellcasting.4.desc: Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.
warlock.spellcasting.5.name: Spellcasting Ability
warlock.spellcasting.5.desc: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.
warlock.spellcasting.6.name: Spellcasting Focus
warlock.spellcasting.6.desc: You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Warlock spells.

For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

wizard.spellcasting.4.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells

wizard.spellcasting.5.name: Spellcasting Ability

wizard.spellcasting.6.name: Spellcasting Focus
